title: Roasted Pepper and Anchovy Salad
subtitle: Charred red and yellow peppers with anchovy, capers and basil
excerpt: Sweet roasted red and yellow peppers stripped of their skins, dressed with anchovy fillets, capers, garlic and basil in olive oil. An Italian antipasto that doubles as a light lunch or a substantial salad course.
sourceNotes: Peperonata and peperoni arrostiti (roasted peppers) are staples of the Italian antipasto tradition, associated particularly with southern Italy and Sicily. The combination of roasted sweet peppers with anchovy, capers and olive oil appears in 20th-century Italian and Italian-American cooking; Elizabeth David included versions in her Italian and French cookery books. The dish came to British cooking through the Italian food revival of the 1970s-1990s.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Bring to room temperature before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a few hours or a day ahead; the flavours deepen as it sits.

content.text: Roasted pepper salad rewards patience. The peppers need to be charred until the skins blister, then rested in a covered bowl until the steam loosens the skin enough to peel. Peeled peppers have a completely different texture to unpeeled ones: silky rather than leathery, with a concentrated sweet flavour. The anchovies dissolve into the oil and season the whole salad without making it taste fishy.

items.prepNote: mixed red and yellow if available
in olive oil, drained and roughly torn

content.text: Heat the oven to 220 C. Place the whole peppers on a baking tray. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and charred in patches. Transfer immediately to a large bowl, cover tightly with clingfilm or a plate, and leave to steam for 15 minutes. The steam loosens the skins. Peel the skins off with your fingers (they should slip off easily), discard the seeds and tear the flesh into wide strips. Collect any juices that run out.

Arrange the pepper strips on a serving dish. Scatter over the {{anchovies}} of torn anchovies, {{capers}} of capers, {{garlic}} of finely sliced garlic and the torn basil. Drizzle over the collected pepper juices, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and {{red-wine-vinegar}} of red wine vinegar. Add {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Do not add salt: the anchovies will season the dish. Taste before adding any.

items.symptom: Skins will not peel off cleanly
items.cause: Not steamed for long enough after roasting.
items.fix: Cover tightly and leave for at least 15 minutes. The steam does the work; peeling immediately just tears the flesh.

items.cause: Anchovies and capers both contribute a lot of salt.
items.fix: Rinse the capers before using. Taste before adding any extra seasoning.

content.text: Roasted peppers with anchovy and capers is a southern Italian antipasto that Elizabeth David brought to British cooks in the 1950s and 1960s. It is one of the most reliable summer starters: it gets better overnight, needs no cooking when served, and belongs on a table with bread and cold wine.
